input: Find a mentor in the UX design field

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing the user's current experience level shapes what kind of mentor they need — a complete beginner needs foundational guidance, while a mid-level designer needs strategic career coaching.
UX design is broad; knowing whether the user wants help with a specific skill (e.g., research, prototyping, portfolio) vs. general career direction changes who the ideal mentor is.
The definition of a successful mentorship varies widely — landing a first job, switching industries, improving a specific skill, or building a network — and determines what to optimize for.
Whether the mentorship is remote or in-person, and the user's location, affects which platforms, communities, and outreach strategies are viable.
Some mentorship programs cost money; knowing the user's budget determines whether paid platforms, free communities, or cold outreach is the right path.
The desired format and frequency of mentorship sessions (weekly calls, async feedback, one-time review) affects which mentors and platforms are a practical fit.

The user may have strong preferences about the mentor's background — e.g., someone in a specific industry (tech, healthcare, agency) or with a particular seniority level — which narrows the search significantly.

gold.taskDescription: The user wants to connect with an experienced UX design professional who can guide their growth in the field.

questions.title: What is your current level of experience in UX design?
questions.description: Understand whether the user is a complete beginner, a career switcher, a student, or a practicing junior/mid-level designer to match them with an appropriately experienced mentor.

questions.title: Which specific area of UX do you want mentorship in?
questions.description: Identify whether the focus is on a particular skill set such as user research, interaction design, portfolio building, or broader career navigation.

questions.title: What is the main outcome you want from this mentorship?
questions.description: Clarify the end goal — e.g., landing a first UX job, getting promoted, breaking into a new industry, or improving a specific deliverable — to define what success looks like.

questions.title: Do you prefer a local in-person mentor or are you open to remote?
questions.description: Determine location preference to decide which platforms, meetups, or communities are relevant for the search.

questions.title: Do you have a budget for paid mentorship platforms or programs?
questions.description: Establish whether the user can use paid services like ADPList Pro, Mentorcruise, or Springboard, or needs to focus on free communities and cold outreach.

questions.title: How often and in what format do you want to meet with a mentor?
questions.description: Find out whether the user wants recurring video calls, async written feedback, a one-time portfolio review, or another format to match them with a compatible mentor.

questions.title: Do you have a preferred industry or background for your mentor?
questions.description: Identify whether the user wants someone from a specific sector (e.g., enterprise tech, startups, agencies, healthcare) or with a particular career path to ensure relevance.
